Annotators shown two full conversations and asked to evaluate models on five criteria including clarification question quality

- Annotators were asked: 'Which one asks better (or more reasonable) clarifying questions?' and evaluated based on Humanness (HU), Engagingness (EG), Interestingness (IN), Knowledgeable (KL), and Clarification (CL).

Annotators are shown two full conversations and asked to answer questions about model performance on Humanness, Engagingness, Interestingness, Knowledgeable, and specifically which model asks better clarifying questions.

We use the four questions that the authors suggest measuring Humanness (HU), Engagingness (EG), Interestingness (IN), Knowledgeable (KL), and add a fifth one, specific to our task, on Clarification (CL).

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated multiple guideline descriptions into one clear summary, normalized criteria naming (fixed 'Engangingness' typo to 'Engagingness') based on paper text

overall_notes: The paper focuses on dialogue generation for clarifying questions in open-domain conversations. It uses both automatic metrics (information retrieval metrics adapted for dialogue evaluation) and human evaluation. No LLM-as-judge evaluation is used. The extraction was generally accurate but needed normalization and consolidation of redundant items.
